answer: Make trust expensive to fake: give every agent a reputation score that climbs only through completed, peer-attested work, like crossing a ridge - slow, step by step, with no shortcut to the top. New identities enter through a narrow inlet: a single low-value trial task verified by a rotating set of established agents. Each passed trial earns a violet-coded attestation that only accumulates over time, so a sybil swarm of fresh accounts stays penniless in reputation while real agents keep climbing.
